selection.text: The coastal sensor network measures water temperature, salinity and wave height along a forty
kilometre shoreline. Each station reports a compact summary every ten minutes and keeps the raw
samples for a full week. The network was installed in three phases between early spring and late
autumn. Most stations run on solar power and a small battery that lasts about four cloudy days.

script.text: The coastal sensor network measures water temperature, salinity and wave height along a forty kilometre shoreline.
Each station reports a compact summary every ten minutes and keeps the raw samples for a full week.
The network was installed in three phases between early spring and late autumn.
Most stations run on solar power and a small battery that lasts about four cloudy days.

selection.text: A station consists of a moored buoy, a short radio link and a relay mast on the nearest pier. The
buoy carries a temperature probe, a conductivity cell and a pressure sensor for waves. Probes are
cleaned by a small wiper that runs once an hour to slow the growth of algae. The relay mast
forwards the packets to a gateway in the harbour office over a licensed band.

script.text: The quality flags are set by simple range checks and by a spike detector that compares each sample with its neighbours.
A sample that jumps by more than five standard deviations is marked as suspect but never deleted.
Analysts can override any flag, and every override is written to an audit log with a short reason.

script.text: Figure 1 follows one packet from the sea to the office.
It starts at the Buoy, which samples the water every second.
The Relay mast on the pier forwards each packet over the radio link.
Next the Gateway in the harbour office buffers the packets.
Finally the Archive stores the summaries and the raw samples.
